concepts.label: SET statement (SQL++ for Analytics, performance parameters)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the Analytics statement that overrides a cluster-wide configuration parameter for one request. Deliberately NOT merged with the promoted n1ql:set-transaction (a different SET-prefixed statement that sets a transaction's isolation level): this SET has no relationship to transactions at all, and the page states it only affects performance, never correctness.

concepts.label: Cost-Based Optimizer (SQL++ for Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - Analytics's own query-plan optimizer, configured through compiler.queryplanshape/compiler.forcejoinorder/compiler.cbo and steered per-query by hint comments. NOT merged with the promoted n1ql:cost-based-optimizer (recurrence 15): no page states the two are the same optimizer, and the tuning surface described here (join build/probe side, zigzag/leftdeep/rightdeep plan shapes, hash broadcast) is specific to Analytics's partitioned-parallel execution model and has no counterpart in the n1ql:cost-based-optimizer record.

concepts.label: Query plan shape (zigzag / leftdeep / rightdeep)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the closed three-value enum for compiler.queryplanshape, governing which side of each hash join in a multi-way join plan is the build side and which is the probe side.

concepts.label: Cost-Based Optimizer hints (SQL++ for Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the family of /*+ ... */ hint comments (productivity, hashjoin, hash-bcast) that steer the Analytics cost-based optimizer for an individual query. NOT merged with the promoted n1ql:optimizer-hints (recurrence 10): the hint syntax, the hint names, and the join-side (build/probe) and broadcast concepts they express are specific to Analytics's own join-execution model, and no page equates the two hint systems.

concepts.label: hash-bcast hint
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a specific optimizer hint that forces one side of an equi-join to be broadcast (replicated) to every partition of the other side, rather than the default partitioned-parallel hash join where both sides are repartitioned on the join key.

relations.subject: analytics:cost-based-optimizer
relations.evidence: The `SET` statement can be used to override some cluster-wide configuration parameters for a specific request

relations.subject: analytics:cost-based-optimizer
relations.evidence: **compiler.queryplanshape**: A string specifying the shape of the query plan produced by the query compiler for multi-way hash join queries. Three settings are available for this parameter: `zigzag`, `leftdeep`, and `rightdeep`.

relations.subject: analytics:cost-based-optimizer
relations.evidence: You can supply hints to the cost-based optimizer using a hint comment. These enable you to specify the behavior of the cost-based optimizer for individual queries.

relations.subject: analytics:optimizer-hints
relations.evidence: Analytics provides the `hash-bcast` join hint to enable this strategy. This hint forces one side of the join to be replicated while the other retains its original partitioning.

relations.subject: analytics:set-statement
relations.evidence: Note that changing query parameters will not affect query correctness but only impact performance characteristics, such as response time and throughput.

notable_absence.finding: None of the compiler.* performance parameters or optimizer hints carry a stated RBAC gate or a version-introduced marker, unlike the Query-service's node/cluster-level settings pages, several of which are role- or version-qualified. All constraints described here are purely behavioral (default values, valid ranges, warning conditions for an invalid hint parameter).

cross_component_finding: This page's tuning surface has no stated relationship to SQL++ for Query's equivalents, but the shapes rhyme closely enough that a reconciler should look rather than assume: this page's per-request SET-based override for compiler.* parameters ('The SET statement can be used to override some cluster-wide configuration parameters for a specific request') mirrors the request-vs-cluster-vs-node layering the registry already models for the Query service via n1ql:request-level-query-parameters/n1ql:cluster-level-query-settings/n1ql:node-level-query-settings - but no page anywhere states the two mechanisms are the same, and Analytics's parameters (compiler.parallelism, compiler.groupmemory/sortmemory/joinmemory/windowmemory, compiler.sort.parallel, compiler.arrayindex, compiler.queryplanshape, compiler.forcejoinorder, compiler.cbo) are named nothing like the Query service's queryXxx-style settings. Left as an observation rather than a relation, since asserting the analogy as a triple would be this agent's inference, not a documented fact.
cross_product_finding: No Capella-specific content appears on this page - no mention of the Query Workbench, Data API, credential types, or any Capella tuning-parameter equivalent.
